claim: COPD ranks as the third leading cause of mortality.
source: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) ranks as the third leading cause of mortality and is projected to account for over a billion deaths by the end of the 21st century (GBD Chronic Respiratory Disease Collaborators, 2020; Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation, 2019; Laniado-Laborín, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (GBD Chronic Respiratory Disease Collaborators, 2020; Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation, 2019; Laniado-Laborín, 2009).

claim: COPD is projected to account for over a billion deaths by the end of the 21st century.
source: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) ranks as the third leading cause of mortality and is projected to account for over a billion deaths by the end of the 21st century (GBD Chronic Respiratory Disease Collaborators, 2020; Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation, 2019; Laniado-Laborín, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (GBD Chronic Respiratory Disease Collaborators, 2020; Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation, 2019; Laniado-Laborín, 2009).

claim: There are currently no treatment options to reverse emphysema.
source: Currently, there are no treatment options to reverse emphysema, the most clinically significant variant of COPD, which often is progressive despite smoking cessation (Bhavani et al., 2015; Anthonisen et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Bhavani et al., 2015; Anthonisen et al., 2002).

claim: Emphysema is the most clinically significant variant of COPD.
source: Currently, there are no treatment options to reverse emphysema, the most clinically significant variant of COPD, which often is progressive despite smoking cessation (Bhavani et al., 2015; Anthonisen et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Bhavani et al., 2015; Anthonisen et al., 2002).

claim: Emphysema is often progressive despite smoking cessation.
source: Currently, there are no treatment options to reverse emphysema, the most clinically significant variant of COPD, which often is progressive despite smoking cessation (Bhavani et al., 2015; Anthonisen et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Bhavani et al., 2015; Anthonisen et al., 2002).

claim: Inhalation of fine particulate matter smaller than 2.5 microns (PM2.5) found in outdoor and indoor air pollution as well as tobacco smoke are risk factors for COPD development.
source: Inhalation of fine particulate matter smaller than 2.5 microns (PM2.5) found in outdoor and indoor air pollution as well as tobacco smoke are risk factors for COPD development (Adeloye et al., 2022; Eisner et al., 2010; Hu et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Adeloye et al., 2022; Eisner et al., 2010; Hu et al., 2010).

claim: Nanosized carbon black (nCB) is a noxious chemical constituent of PM2.5 found in the lungs of smokers.
source: We have previously shown that nanosized carbon black (nCB), a noxious chemical constituent of PM2.5 found in the lungs of smokers, activates macrophages and dendritic cells orchestrating a pathogenic T cell-dependent inflammatory response and emphysema in mice (Lu et al., 2015; You et al., 2015; Shan et al., 2009; Chang et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Lu et al., 2015; You et al., 2015; Shan et al., 2009; Chang et al., 2022).

claim: Nanosized carbon black activates macrophages and dendritic cells orchestrating a pathogenic T cell-dependent inflammatory response and emphysema in mice.
source: We have previously shown that nanosized carbon black (nCB), a noxious chemical constituent of PM2.5 found in the lungs of smokers, activates macrophages and dendritic cells orchestrating a pathogenic T cell-dependent inflammatory response and emphysema in mice (Lu et al., 2015; You et al., 2015; Shan et al., 2009; Chang et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Lu et al., 2015; You et al., 2015; Shan et al., 2009; Chang et al., 2022).

claim: Aberrant T cells are implicated in impaired host defense, exaggerated inflammation, and loss of self-tolerance in COPD.
source: Aberrant T cells are implicated in impaired host defense, exaggerated inflammation, and loss of self-tolerance in COPD (Williams et al., 2021; Chen et al., 2023; Hogg et al., 2004; Maeno et al., 2007; Xu et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Williams et al., 2021; Chen et al., 2023; Hogg et al., 2004; Maeno et al., 2007; Xu et al., 2012).

claim: Activated IFN-γ and IL-17-secreting subsets of CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes including Th1, Th17, and Tc1 cells are pathogenic in COPD.
source: In this regard, we and others have demonstrated the role and pathogenicity of activated IFN-γ and IL-17-secreting subsets of CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes including Th1, Th17, and Tc1 cells in clinical isolates and in mice with COPD (Lu et al., 2015; You et al., 2015; Shan et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2007; Kheradmand et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Lu et al., 2015; You et al., 2015; Shan et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2007; Kheradmand et al., 2023).

claim: IL-17-secreting Th17 cells promote the destruction of lung epithelium and recruitment of macrophages and neutrophils which then release proteolytic enzymes such as matrix metalloproteinases involved in the degradation of the lung structural matrix.
source: The IL-17-secreting Th17 cells are particularly important as they promote the destruction of lung epithelium and recruitment of macrophages and neutrophils which then release proteolytic enzymes such as matrix metalloproteinases involved in the degradation of the lung structural matrix (Barnes, 2016; Hoenderdos and Condliffe, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Barnes, 2016; Hoenderdos and Condliffe, 2013).

claim: Intranasal inhalation of nCB in mice is sufficient to induce emphysema by stimulating lung T cell activation by dendritic cells and macrophages.
source: We previously demonstrated that intranasal inhalation of nCB in mice is sufficient to induce emphysema by stimulating lung T cell activation by dendritic cells and macrophages.
evidence: Based on prior work by the authors.

claim: Genetic ablation of IL-17A can attenuate nCB- or cigarette smoke (CS)-induced alveolar destruction and airway inflammation.
source: Moreover, we found that genetic ablation of IL-17A can attenuate nCB- or cigarette smoke (CS)-induced alveolar destruction and airway inflammation (Shan et al., 2012; You et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Shan et al., 2012; You et al., 2015).

claim: IL-17A- and IL-17F-secreting CD8+ T cell (Tc17) subpopulation plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of several autoimmune and inflammatory disorders.
source: More recently, IL-17A- and IL-17F-secreting CD8+ T cell (Tc17) subpopulation has been shown to play a critical role in the pathogenesis of several autoimmune and inflammatory disorders (Globig et al., 2022; Huber et al., 2013; Srenathan et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Globig et al., 2022; Huber et al., 2013; Srenathan et al., 2016).

claim: Both Th17 and Tc17 require the fate-deterministic transcription factor RAR-related orphan receptor gamma t (RORγt, encoded by Rorc) for differentiation and production of IL-17A.
source: Both Th17 and Tc17 require the fate-deterministic transcription factor RAR-related orphan receptor gamma t (RORγt, encoded by Rorc) for differentiation and production of IL-17A (Ivanov et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Ivanov et al., 2007).

claim: RORγt is the best-studied positive transcriptional regulator of IL-17A and IL-17F.
source: RORγt is the best-studied positive transcriptional regulator of IL-17A and IL-17F (Ivanov et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Ivanov et al., 2006).

claim: RORγt expression has been reported to be elevated in COPD patients and in mouse models of COPD.
source: In accordance with the importance of IL-17A transcription, RORγt expression has also been reported to be elevated in COPD patients and in mouse models of COPD (Chu et al., 2011; Li et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Chu et al., 2011; Li et al., 2015).

claim: Mir22 inhibits HDAC4, promoting antigen-presenting cell (APC) activation in the lungs and inducing Th17-mediated emphysema in response to CS or nCB in mice.
source: We previously reported that Mir22 inhibits HDAC4, promoting antigen-presenting cell (APC) activation in the lungs and inducing Th17-mediated emphysema in response to CS or nCB in mice (Lu et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Lu et al., 2015).

claim: The Mirlet7 family controls APC and/or T cell-driven IL-17A+ inflammation.
source: Additional microRNAs (miRNAs) that control APC and/or T cell-driven IL-17A+ inflammation have been identified by others including the Mirlet7 family (Yang, 2012; Angelou et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Yang, 2012; Angelou et al., 2019).

claim: Members of the Mirlet7 family, including Mirlet7a, Mirlet7b, Mirlet7c, Mirlet7d, Mirlet7e, and Mirlet7f are frequently downregulated in human emphysematous lung tissue and in murine models of emphysema.
source: miRNA expression-based studies have shown frequent downregulation of members of the Mirlet7 family, including Mirlet7a, Mirlet7b, Mirlet7c, Mirlet7d, Mirlet7e, and Mirlet7f in human emphysematous lung tissue and in murine models of emphysema, but the mechanism(s) of action remain ill-defined (Christenson et al., 2013; Pottelberge et al., 2011; Conickx et al., 2017; Izzotti et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Christenson et al., 2013; Pottelberge et al., 2011; Conickx et al., 2017; Izzotti et al., 2009).

claim: Mirlet7 genes are encoded across eight loci either as single genes or as polycistronic clusters.
source: Mirlet7 genes are encoded across eight loci either as single genes or as polycistronic clusters which have confounded their analysis in vivo (Rodriguez et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Rodriguez et al., 2004).

claim: Lin28b transgenic overexpression in T cells blocks the maturation and processing of the Mirlet7 family.
source: Previous studies used Lin28b transgenic overexpression in T cells to block the maturation and processing of the Mirlet7 family.
evidence: Based on prior published studies.

claim: Mirlet7 family has an inhibitory role in Th17-driven response in the murine model of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis attributed in part to regulation of IL-1 receptor 1 and IL-23 receptor.
source: They showed an inhibitory role of Mirlet7 family in Th17-driven response in the murine model of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis attributed in part to regulation of IL-1 receptor 1 and IL-23 receptor (Angelou et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to published literature (Angelou et al., 2019).

claim: MIRLET7A3/MIRLET7B and MIRLET7A1/MIRLET7F1/MIRLET7D clusters are suppressed in the T cells isolated from lungs of emphysema patients.
source: Here, we found that MIRLET7, notably the MIRLET7A3/MIRLET7B and MIRLET7A1/MIRLET7F1/MIRLET7D clusters, are suppressed in the T cells isolated from lungs of emphysema patients.
evidence: Based on data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The murine Mirlet7b/Mirlet7c2 and Mirlet7a1/Mirlet7f1/Mirlet7d clusters were downregulated in pre-clinical emphysema models.
source: Consistently, the analogous murine Mirlet7b/Mirlet7c2 and Mirlet7a1/Mirlet7f1/Mirlet7d clusters, respectively, were similarly downregulated in pre-clinical emphysema models.
evidence: Based on data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Deletion of Mirlet7 miRNA in T cells worsened alveolar damage elicited by inhalation of CS or nCB.
source: Deletion of Mirlet7 miRNA in T cells worsened alveolar damage elicited by inhalation of CS or nCB, and increased infiltration of immune cells in the airways, including IL-17-producing CD8+ T (Tc17) cells.
evidence: Based on data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Deletion of Mirlet7 miRNA in T cells increased infiltration of immune cells in the airways, including IL-17-producing CD8+ T (Tc17) cells.
source: Deletion of Mirlet7 miRNA in T cells worsened alveolar damage elicited by inhalation of CS or nCB, and increased infiltration of immune cells in the airways, including IL-17-producing CD8+ T (Tc17) cells.
evidence: Based on data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Mirlet7 controls type 17 differentiation by directly targeting the lineage-determining transcription factor, RORγt.
source: Mechanistically, we found that Mirlet7 controls type 17 differentiation by directly targeting the lineage-determining transcription factor, RORγt.
evidence: Based on data presented in the manuscript including luciferase reporter assays.

claim: Mirlet7 GOF mice were resistant to nCB-mediated induction of RORγt and Tc17 responses.
source: In support of this conclusion, Mirlet7 GOF mice were resistant to nCB-mediated induction of RORγt and Tc17 responses.
evidence: Based on data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Mirlet7 acts as a repressor of RORγt.
source: Thus, we show a previously unappreciated role for Mirlet7 as a repressor of RORγt and a molecular brake to the IL-17-mediated T cell inflammation in emphysema.
evidence: Based on data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Mirlet7 acts as a molecular brake to the IL-17-mediated T cell inflammation in emphysema.
source: Thus, we show a previously unappreciated role for Mirlet7 as a repressor of RORγt and a molecular brake to the IL-17-mediated T cell inflammation in emphysema.
evidence: Based on data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The Mirlet7ahg and Mirlet7bhg gene cluster transcripts are significantly downregulated in COPD compared to control subjects.
source: Our analysis identified significant downregulation of the Mirlet7ahg and Mirlet7bhg gene cluster transcripts in COPD compared to control subjects (Figure 1B).
evidence: Based on analysis of published RNA-seq dataset (GSE57148) shown in Figure 1B.

claim: MIRLET7A is significantly downregulated in emphysema samples relative to controls.
source: We carried out quantitative PCR (qPCR) detection of MIRLET7A, which is encoded by both clusters, in lung tissue samples of smokers with emphysema and non-emphysema controls, detecting significant downregulation of MIRLET7A in emphysema samples relative to controls (Figure 1C).
evidence: Based on qPCR data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The CD4+ T cell expression of Mirlet7a, Mirlet7b, Mirlet7d, and Mirlet7f are all inversely correlated with more severe emphysema distribution in the lungs as determined by Computed Tomography (CT) scan.
source: In support of our original hypothesis, the CD4+ T cell expression of Mirlet7a, Mirlet7b, Mirlet7d, and Mirlet7f were all inversely correlated with more severe emphysema distribution in the lungs as determined by Computed Tomography (CT) scan (Figure 1D).
evidence: Based on qPCR and regression analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Mice with CS- or nCB-induced emphysema exhibited reduced expression levels of pri-Mirlet7b/c2 and pri-Mirlet7a1/f1/d transcripts in the lung.
source: Paralleling our observations in human COPD and emphysema, mice with CS- or nCB-induced emphysema exhibited reduced expression levels of pri-Mirlet7b/c2 and pri-Mirlet7a1/f1/d transcripts in the lung and from isolated lung CD4+ and CD8+ T cells (Figure 1F–H).
evidence: Based on qPCR data shown in Figure 1F-H.

claim: Mice with CS- or nCB-induced emphysema exhibited reduced expression levels of pri-Mirlet7b/c2 and pri-Mirlet7a1/f1/d transcripts from isolated lung CD4+ and CD8+ T cells.
source: Paralleling our observations in human COPD and emphysema, mice with CS- or nCB-induced emphysema exhibited reduced expression levels of pri-Mirlet7b/c2 and pri-Mirlet7a1/f1/d transcripts in the lung and from isolated lung CD4+ and CD8+ T cells (Figure 1F–H).
evidence: Based on qPCR data shown in Figure 1F-H.

claim: let7bc2LOF mice exhibit robust conditional deletion of Mirlet7bc2 in DP thymocytes and peripheral T cells.
source: We confirmed that let7bc2LOF mice exhibit robust conditional deletion of Mirlet7bc2 in DP thymocytes and peripheral T cells (Figure 2B and data not shown).
evidence: Based on qPCR data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: let7bc2LOF adult mice were born at the expected Mendelian frequency.
source: Our let7bc2LOF adult mice were born at the expected Mendelian frequency and did not show any overt histopathologic or inflammatory changes in lungs histopathology up to 1 year of age in comparison to let7bc2f/f control mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: Based on observations and data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: let7bc2LOF adult mice did not show any overt histopathologic or inflammatory changes in lungs histopathology up to 1 year of age in comparison to let7bc2f/f control mice.
source: Our let7bc2LOF adult mice were born at the expected Mendelian frequency and did not show any overt histopathologic or inflammatory changes in lungs histopathology up to 1 year of age in comparison to let7bc2f/f control mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: Based on observations and data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: Quantification of major immune populations and T cell subsets by flow cytometry in let7bc2LOF were comparable to control mice under baseline conditions and with moderate aging.
source: Furthermore, quantification of major immune populations and T cell subsets by flow cytometry in let7bc2LOF were comparable to control mice under baseline conditions and with moderate aging (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: Based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, D.

claim: The enlargement of alveolar spaces sustained from either nCB or CS exposure was exaggerated in let7bc2LOF mice relative to controls.
source: Histomorphometry measurements of mean linear intercept (MLI) from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained sections revealed that the enlargement of alveolar spaces sustained from either nCB or CS exposure was exaggerated in let7bc2LOF mice relative to controls (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: Based on MLI measurements shown in Figure 2C–E.

claim: let7bc2LOF mice treated with nCB showed significantly increased airway infiltration of macrophages and neutrophils in BAL fluid as compared to wild-type control animals.
source: Internally consistent with MLI measurements, let7bc2LOF mice treated with nCB showed significantly increased airway infiltration of macrophages and neutrophils in BAL fluid as compared to wild-type control animals (Figure 2F).
evidence: Based on BAL fluid cell counts shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Expression levels of Mmp9 and Mmp12 were elevated in airways of let7bc2LOF mice exposed to CS versus controls.
source: Concomitant with these findings, expression levels of Mmp9 and Mmp12, which are secreted by macrophages and neutrophils to degrade elastin and mediate alveolar damage, were elevated in airways of let7bc2LOF mice exposed to CS versus controls (Figure 2G).
evidence: Based on mRNA expression data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Mmp9 and Mmp12 are secreted by macrophages and neutrophils to degrade elastin and mediate alveolar damage.
source: Concomitant with these findings, expression levels of Mmp9 and Mmp12, which are secreted by macrophages and neutrophils to degrade elastin and mediate alveolar damage, were elevated in airways of let7bc2LOF mice exposed to CS versus controls (Figure 2G).
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about Mmp9 and Mmp12 function.

claim: let7bc2LOF mice treated with nCB exhibit significantly less pri-Mirlet7b/c2 transcript expression in isolated lung T cells relative to wild-type control mice.
source: As expected, let7bc2LOF mice treated with nCB exhibit significantly less pri-Mirlet7b/c2 transcript expression in isolated lung T cells relative to wild-type control mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and data not shown).
evidence: Based on qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The Mirlet7bc2 cluster within T cells protects by dampening airway destruction and inflammation because the absence of this cluster worsens the severity of experimental emphysema in mice.
source: Collectively, our data suggest that the Mirlet7bc2 cluster within T cells protects by dampening airway destruction and inflammation because the absence of this cluster worsens the severity of experimental emphysema in mice.
evidence: Based on inference from the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: nCB elicits enriched proportions and counts of Tc1/Tc17 as well as Th1/Th17 cells in wild-type mice.
source: The flow cytometric profiling of lung T cells revealed enriched proportions and counts of Tc1/Tc17 as well as Th1/Th17 cells in wild-type mice upon treatment with nCB (Figure 3A, B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3A, B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: nCB elicits both the type 17 and type 1 T cell responses, consistent with CS and elastase pre-clinical models of emphysema.
source: These findings suggests that nCB elicits both the type 17 and type 1T cell responses, consistent with CS and elastase pre-clinical models of emphysema (Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: Based on data presented in the manuscript and citation to published literature (Zhang et al., 2019).

claim: let7bc2LOF mice showed increased CD8+IL17A+ Tc17 cells relative to nCB control animals.
source: Interestingly, let7bc2LOF mice showed increased CD8+IL17A+ Tc17 cells relative to nCB control animals.
evidence: Based on data presented in the manuscript.

claim: CD8+IFNγ+ and GZMA+ Tc1 populations remained unperturbed with absence of Mirlet7bc2.
source: In contrast, CD8+IFNγ+ and GZMA+ Tc1 populations remained unperturbed with absence of Mirlet7bc2, suggestive of a more refined regulatory role on Tc17 differentiation (Figure 3A, B).
evidence: Based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3A, B.

claim: There were no significant differences in either Th1 or Th17 cells when comparing nCB-treated let7bc2LOF to wild-type controls.
source: There were no significant differences in either Th1 or Th17 cells when comparing nCB-treated let7bc2LOF to wild-type controls, indicating the Mirlet7bc2 was dispensable for their generation (Figure 3C).
evidence: Based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Mirlet7bc2 was dispensable for Th1 or Th17 cell generation.
source: There were no significant differences in either Th1 or Th17 cells when comparing nCB-treated let7bc2LOF to wild-type controls, indicating the Mirlet7bc2 was dispensable for their generation (Figure 3C).
evidence: Based on inference from flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Regulatory T cells form a dynamic axis with Tc17/Th17 cells and act as a counterbalance to lung inflammation in emphysema.
source: Regulatory T cells form a dynamic axis with Tc17/Th17 cells and act as a counterbalance to lung inflammation in emphysema (Duan et al., 2016; Jin et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Duan et al., 2016; Jin et al., 2014).

claim: The let7bc2LOF mice showed no significant difference in the Tregs subset relative to controls in the nCB emphysema model.
source: The let7bc2LOF mice showed no significant difference in the Tregs subset relative to controls in our model (Figure 3D).
evidence: Based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Deletion of Mirlet7bc2 is insufficient to provoke Tc17 cell generation under homeostatic conditions.
source: Together, our data support the notion that deletion of Mirlet7bc2 is insufficient to provoke Tc17 cell generation under homeostatic conditions.
evidence: Based on inference from the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Under the context of chronic inflammation in emphysema, the loss of the Mirlet7bc2 cluster is intrinsic for the potentiation of T cells toward Tc17 differentiation.
source: However, under the context of chronic inflammation in emphysema, the loss of the Mirlet7bc2 cluster is intrinsic for the potentiation of T cells toward Tc17 differentiation.
evidence: Based on inference from the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The 3′UTR region of Rorc, encoding RORγt, contains an evolutionarily conserved and complementary motif for the Mirlet7 family.
source: This analysis revealed that the 3′UTR region of Rorc, encoding RORγt, contains an evolutionarily conserved and complementary motif for the Mirlet7 family (Figure 4A).
evidence: Based on TargetScan predictive algorithm analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: let7bc2LOF mice showed induction of RORγt in single-positive CD8+ and CD4+ thymocytes, as well as peripheral splenic CD8+ and CD4+ T cells.
source: Our interrogation of RORγt mean fluorescent intensity (MFI) by flow cytometry showed induction of RORγt in single-positive CD8+ and CD4+ thymocytes, as well as peripheral splenic CD8+ and CD4+ T cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: Based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: RORγt levels appeared unchanged in purified lung CD8+ T cells and CD4+ T cells of naive let7bc2LOF mice.
source: However, RORγt levels appeared unchanged in purified lung CD8+ T cells and CD4+ T cells of naive let7bc2LOF mice, alluding to a compensatory effect in homeostatic lung T cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: Based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: nCB-emphysematous let7bc2LOF mice exhibited enhanced RORγt protein levels in both CD8+ and CD4+ T cells relative to control mice with emphysema.
source: Indeed, nCB-emphysematous let7bc2LOF mice exhibited enhanced RORγt protein levels in both CD8+ and CD4+ T cells relative to control mice with emphysema (Figure 4C).
evidence: Based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The let7afdLOF mice aged up to 6 months did not exhibit overt lung histopathology and inflammatory changes.
source: The let7afdLOF mice aged up to 6 months did not exhibit overt lung histopathology and inflammatory changes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–E).
evidence: Based on observations and data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–E.

claim: Ablation of Mirlet7afd enhanced levels of RORγt in thymic and peripheral T cells of mice.
source: Of particular interest, ablation of Mirlet7afd enhanced levels of RORγt in thymic and peripheral T cells of mice (Figure 4D).
evidence: Based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Independent Mirlet7 clusters restrain RORγt expression levels from thymic development to peripheral T cells under homeostatic conditions.
source: Overall, this indicates that independent Mirlet7 clusters restrain RORγt expression levels from thymic development to peripheral T cells under homeostatic conditions.
evidence: Based on inference from the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Intranasal administration of nCB provoked increased RORγt expression in lung T cells of let7afdLOF mice compared to control mice.
source: Intranasal administration of nCB provoked increased RORγt expression in lung T cells of let7afdLOF mice compared to control mice (Figure 4E), supporting overlapping functionality between the Mirlet7bc2 and Mirlet7afd in repression of RORγt within T cells.
evidence: Based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: There is overlapping functionality between the Mirlet7bc2 and Mirlet7afd in repression of RORγt within T cells.
source: Intranasal administration of nCB provoked increased RORγt expression in lung T cells of let7afdLOF mice compared to control mice (Figure 4E), supporting overlapping functionality between the Mirlet7bc2 and Mirlet7afd in repression of RORγt within T cells.
evidence: Based on inference from the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Mirlet7bc2 deficient CD8+ T cells showed enhanced commitment toward Tc17 cells and IL-17A+ production relative to control CD8+ T cells.
source: Our flow cytometric analysis confirmed the enhanced commitment of Mirlet7bc2 deficient CD8+ T cells toward Tc17 cells and IL-17A+ production relative to control CD8+ T cells (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: Based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5A, B.

claim: Enhanced Tc17 cell differentiation mirrored the increased IL-17A detected in the supernatant from in vitro polarized cells.
source: Moreover, enhanced Tc17 cell differentiation mirrored the increased IL-17A detected in the supernatant from in vitro polarized cells as quantified by ELISA (Figure 5C).
evidence: Based on ELISA data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Parallel assessment of Tc1 differentiation did not detect a difference in CD8+IFNγ+ cells between let7bc2LOF and control.
source: Parallel assessment of Tc1 differentiation did not detect a difference in CD8+IFNγ+ cells (Figure 5A and D).
evidence: Based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5A and D.

claim: The Mirlet7bc2 cluster negatively regulates Tc17 response but is dispensable in Tc1 cells.
source: Altogether, these data recapitulated our in vivo findings that the Mirlet7bc2 cluster negatively regulates Tc17 response but is dispensable in Tc1 cells.
evidence: Based on inference from the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Absence of Mirlet7afd in T cells enhanced differentiation toward Tc17 cells.
source: As we had observed with let7bc2LOF, absence of Mirlet7afd in T cells further enhanced differentiation toward Tc17 cells as quantified by flow cytometry and ELISA (Figure 5F, G).
evidence: Based on flow cytometry and ELISA data shown in Figure 5F, G.

claim: RORγt expression was differentially and significantly upregulated under both Tc0 and Tc17 differentiation conditions in Mirlet7 LOF cells relative to controls.
source: In agreement with enhanced Tc17 differentiation, RORγt expression was differentially and significantly upregulated under both Tc0 and Tc17 differentiation conditions in Mirlet7 LOF cells relative to controls (Figure 5E, H).
evidence: Based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5E, H.

claim: Mirlet7b represses Rorc.
source: These reporter assays with Mirlet7b expressing cells independently confirmed that Mirlet7b represses Rorc (Figure 5I, left).
evidence: Based on luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Deletion of the putative Mirlet7-binding sequence abrogated repression by Mirlet7b.
source: Furthermore, deletion of the putative Mirlet7-binding sequence (Figure 4A) abrogated repression by Mirlet7b (Figure 5I, right), thus confirming Rorc as a functional target.
evidence: Based on luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Rorc is a functional target of Mirlet7.
source: Furthermore, deletion of the putative Mirlet7-binding sequence (Figure 4A) abrogated repression by Mirlet7b (Figure 5I, right), thus confirming Rorc as a functional target.
evidence: Based on inference from luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Mirlet7 has an upstream regulatory role in Tc17 differentiation, mediated in part, via direct suppression of RORγt.
source: Overall, these in vitro experiments readily recapitulated an upstream regulatory role of Mirlet7 in Tc17 differentiation, mediated in part, via direct suppression of RORγt.
evidence: Based on inference from the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The rtTA-iLet7 mouse model has been utilized to promote ~two- to threefold rise in total Mirlet7 activity in T cells.
source: The rtTA-iLet7 mouse model has been utilized to promote ~two- to threefold rise in total Mirlet7 activity in T cells (Angelou et al., 2019; Wells et al., 2017; Wells et al., 2023; Angelou et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to published literature (Angelou et al., 2019; Wells et al., 2017; Wells et al., 2023; Angelou et al., 2019).

claim: Mirlet7 acts as a molecular brake to the type 17 T cell response through the direct regulation of RORγt.
